corpus.note: Candidates in candidates.json were captured by replaying the production FTS path (searchsql.SQLiteBackend.Query with rank.FetchLimit(10)) against that graph; intent_candidates.json was captured the same way through Reader.QueryIntent. Both captures are frozen: they never re-read a database, so a metric change is attributable to the search service alone.

authorship.written_by: assistant, 2026-08-08, before running any measurement; 47 intent questions merged in 2026-08-10 from the retired intent golden set, keeping their original file-level judgments as relevant_files
authorship.caveat: The same author wrote the ranker and these judgments, so the set cannot prove the ranking is good. It can prove a later change made it worse. Expectations are never edited to make a run pass; a failing query is either a real defect or a documented disagreement.

label_format: kind:qualified_name@file_path — `search` is scored on the node, `wiki_search` on the file after the @

queries.query: SanitizeFTS5
queries.why: The full identifier, typed exactly. Nothing else can be meant.

queries.query: BuildContent
queries.why: Only one node carries this name.

queries.query: UnresolvedEdgeCandidate
queries.why: Long unique type name; an exact hit is the only acceptable answer.

queries.query: promoteExactNameMatch
queries.why: Unexported but uniquely named.

queries.query: RunMigrations
queries.why: Unique exported entry point.

queries.query: sanit
queries.why: Half-typed prefix. Every sanitize* function in the graph is a fair first hit, including gitrepo.sanitizeURL. An earlier judgment excluded sanitizeURL as 'a different subject', which asked the ranker to know which sanitizer the typist had in mind from five shared letters. Nothing in the query says. A prefix this short names a family, not a member. Membership updated 2026-08-10: sanitizeTokens and sanitizeRawTokens were deleted when token normalization was unified, and the intent-index sanitizers (SanitizeIntentFTS5, SanitizePostgresIntentTSQuery) joined the family.

queries.query: rerank
queries.why: Exactly one node spells this.

queries.query: annot
queries.why: Short prefix over a crowded namespace. The domain type or its own package files are what someone typing five letters wants, not an MCP response DTO.

queries.query: crossref
queries.why: The domain type and the service that owns the feature outrank the persistence and transport shells.

queries.query: impact
queries.why: One word naming a whole feature. The analyzer, its file, or its package all answer it.

queries.query: discovery
queries.why: Someone asking about discovery wants to learn what package discovery is here: the interface that names the idea, and the file that holds it. The nine language-specific implementations are what that idea expands into, not the answer to the question. An earlier judgment said this query existed to 'test the free-prefix rule', which is a scoring rule and not something a person wants; the list has to answer what the person wanted. Two problems sit behind it. treesitter.PackageDiscovery, the interface, is not in the candidate pool at all, so retrieval loses it before any ranking runs. And the pool holds nine near-identical siblings that fill the top of the result on their own.

queries.query: syncer
queries.why: Trailing word shared by one concrete type and several interfaces.

queries.query: radius
queries.why: The word only exists inside the impact feature, so anything in that file is a fair hit.

queries.query: tracer
queries.why: The flow tracer, not the observability trace file, which spells the word differently.

queries.query: membership
queries.why: Trailing word of exactly one domain type.

queries.query: fts
queries.why: Uppercase run inside a longer name. This is the case isAcronymTail was added for.

queries.query: sqlite
queries.why: Mixed-case acronym followed by a word: the SQLiteBackend spelling.

queries.query: mcp
queries.why: A three-letter acronym naming a whole adapter. The package node is the answer; nothing smaller is. An earlier judgment also accepted mcp/deps.go, which cannot be defended: the pool holds about twenty-five files from that same package and deps.go is not distinguished from any of them. Judging one and not its siblings measured nothing. The package node is not in the candidate pool, so this query is now a retrieval finding, not a ranking one: no reordering can answer it while the only correct node never arrives.

queries.query: cfg
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose. No node is named cfg — it only ever appears as a local variable, and locals are not indexed — so the query can only be answered by guessing that cfg means config. Measured over the whole graph, cfg scores config 0.28 against a 0.08 ceiling for unrelated junk: a margin too thin to build a gate on.

queries.query: parsecache
queries.why: Written as one word by the user, stored as three spellings in the graph: ParseCache, parsecache.go, parse_cache.go. Tests that case and separator style do not decide the answer. Filed under subword, not abbreviation: nothing is abbreviated, only respelled, and averaging it with cfg made the abbreviation bucket read 0.500 when the two queries measure different things.

queries.query: sanitze
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose. Dropped an 'i', which subsequence matching still sees, so this one is reachable — but only through the qualified name; FTS returns no candidate for it at all. See the bucket note.

queries.query: retreival
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose. Swapped 'ie' for 'ei'. A transposition breaks the ordered subsequence outright, so no amount of ranking can recover it — only edit-distance matching could, and that was removed.

queries.query: anotation
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose. One 'n' short. Still an ordered subsequence of annotation, but FTS never returns the candidate, so the ranker is never given the chance.

queries.query: package discovery
queries.why: Two words typed with a space for an identifier written camelCase.

queries.query: impact radius
queries.why: Names the feature the way the docs do; the analyzer method is the implementation.

queries.query: cross ref
queries.why: Split across two tokens by the user, joined in the code.

queries.query: trace flow
queries.why: This is also the name of an MCP tool, so the DTOs in handler_analysis.go compete with the real implementation.

queries.query: search document
queries.why: Two things in this repository answer to the name and both are correct. graph.SearchDocument is the stored row; internal/app/search/document builds its content. An earlier judgment recognised only the second and called the first wrong, which cannot hold against a type spelled exactly as the query. It also claimed path and name evidence point the same way here, and they do not: BuildContent carries neither word in its name and is reachable only through its path.

queries.query: flow membership
queries.why: One domain type, spelled as two words.

queries.query: incremental syncer
queries.why: The concrete Syncer splits its two words across package and type name; the interface joins them.

queries.query: treesitter semantics
queries.why: One word is a directory, the other is a name. Path evidence should break ties here, not override the name.

queries.query: graphgorm crossref
queries.why: The package name narrows a feature that exists in four packages. An earlier judgment accepted only the contents of crossref.go, which drew the line at a filename the query never mentions: graphgorm.crossRefEdges is in the named package and is about cross-references, so it satisfies both words as well as anything in crossref.go does.

queries.query: migration schema
queries.why: Both words are in the identifier and one is in the path.

queries.query: worker pool
queries.why: Two words describing a shape rather than naming a symbol. Both answers were read in the source, not taken from their summaries: queue.go:206-208 starts `workers` goroutines running q.worker(), and build.go:335-362 spawns workerCount goroutines draining a jobs channel. Neither node carries the words in its name or its path, so today both score zero on name and zero on path and the retrieval order alone decides. The pool holds two candidates and both are relevant, so this query records the shape; it cannot discriminate between rankings.

queries.query: bounded traversal
queries.why: Describes what the code does. These two are the graph walks that take explicit caps; the other three candidates in the pool report or configure a bounded walk rather than performing one. Both answers spell Bounded in their names, so name evidence already reaches them.

queries.query: how does the graph get built
queries.why: A whole question, the shape a person or an agent types when it does not know the symbol name. Build is the full-build entry point (build.go:155: walks source files, stores parsed graph data, rebuilds search docs). `search` returns nothing for it and the cause is measured, not guessed: SanitizeFTS5 joins its terms with a space (sanitize.go:47), and a space is FTS5's implicit AND, so every remaining word must appear in one document. Every query of five words or more tested against this graph returned zero candidates there. That is why `search` declines the whole bucket. `wiki_search` answers it from the namespace scan, and is scored on it: build.go was 6th, and 2nd once the scan stopped counting `the` as evidence.

queries.query: what happens when a webhook arrives
queries.why: ServeHTTP is the entry point a push event lands on: it validates the event and dispatches repository sync. Zero candidates in `search`, for the same reason as the rest of the bucket. `wiki_search` shows handler.go first.

queries.query: where do search results get ranked
queries.why: Rerank is the single ordering entry point; every search path funnels into it. Zero candidates in `search`. `wiki_search` reaches rank.go but does not fit it on a page of ten: the query's own words — search, results, get — are spread across every file that has a search API, and rank.go's surface says `Rerank`, not `ranked`. This is the hardest question in the set and the one left open.

queries.query: how do i follow a call chain
queries.why: Describes call-flow tracing without using the words trace or flow, which is the point: the searcher does not know the name. Zero candidates in `search`. In `wiki_search` flow.go was 1st and is now 2nd: it used to win partly on `a`, `do`, `i` and `how`, and once those stopped being evidence it lost the top spot to semantics_js_ts.go, which matches `call chain` on its own surface. The trade was accepted — the words it lost were not about this question.

queries.query: what stops the server accepting new work
queries.why: Shutdown stops accepting new work and waits for workers to finish or time out (queue.go:259-262). Zero candidates in `search`. `wiki_search` shows queue.go first, on the strength of its @intent line.

queries.query: syncqueue
queries.why: A type name typed on its own. The type itself is the obvious answer, and its exported methods are what the type is for: naming a type is how a searcher asks what it can do. Written before measuring, and expected red today: the ranker scores a node's own name and the last segment of its qualified name, both of which are the method name, so the receiver type never enters the score and SyncQueue.Add looks unrelated to the word syncqueue.

queries.query: webhookhandler
queries.why: The type has exactly two methods and both are the substance of it: ServeHTTP is where a push event lands, verifySignature is the check that runs before anything is trusted. verifySignature is unexported and still relevant — the query names the type, and a reader asking what this handler does needs the check as much as the entry point.

queries.query: sqlitebackend
queries.why: Same shape with a larger method set, so it also measures whether fixing the receiver gap floods the list: this type has nine methods and only these five are its interface. The four unexported ones (rebuildTable, rebuildTableNodes, upgradeLegacyFTSTable, and the rest) are implementation detail of Rebuild and are not counted as answers.

queries.query: zzz nonexistent symbol qqq
queries.why: Nothing may be returned. Guards against a scorer that always finds something. Under wiki_search this used to return ten files, every one of them matching `symbol` alone while `zzz`, `nonexistent`, and `qqq` matched nothing anywhere; it returns none since the scan learned to decline a query whose words mostly name nothing.

queries.query: what stops two pushes for the same repository from building at the same time
queries.why: checkout.go records that git work is serialized per repository across concurrent webhook deliveries, and queue.go records that bursty pushes for one repository are coalesced. Either file is a place the reader can start walking.

queries.query: who checks that a push really came from the forge before we trust it
queries.why: handler.go records authenticating webhook payloads before the sync pipeline trusts their repository metadata. Nothing else records a reason about proving where a delivery came from.

queries.query: why did a failing sync stop retrying instead of backing off again
queries.why: queue.go records wrapping permanent failures so retry backoff short-circuits. The wrapper and the retry loop live in the same file, so one hit is enough to walk both.

queries.query: how does a sync that is already running end when the server is told to stop
queries.why: queue.go records both cancelling retries and worker waits and giving in-flight webhook sync a bounded graceful exit.

queries.query: what refuses to read a file that sits outside the documentation directory
queries.why: all three record rejecting traversal and symlink escape before a read. They are separate entry points for the MCP tool, the namespace-scoped read, and the Wiki server, and any of them starts the reader in the right place.

queries.query: what keeps a parser result from being reused after the file it came from changed
queries.why: store.go records preventing stale parser output from being reused across content, path, parser, context, or namespace changes; walker.go records bumping the key when language queries change. The cache key is written in one and invalidated in the other.

queries.query: why does a result say it was cut short instead of returning everything
queries.why: each of these records reporting truncation next to the bounded result it produced. The reader is looking for whichever surface truncated, so all four are acceptable starts.

queries.query: what stops one repository from filling a result that covers several
queries.why: handler_query.go records keeping one high-scoring repository from starving the other namespaces out of a federated result.

queries.query: why was a push that only deleted a branch ignored
queries.why: handler.go records skipping pushes that report branch deletion instead of a syncable commit head.

queries.query: what decides which repositories and branches are allowed to sync
queries.why: admission.go records the whole allowlist decision: repo rules, branch globs, and the order later rules override earlier ones.

queries.query: why is a lock file left behind by a crashed run eventually cleaned up
queries.why: checkout.go records writing lock provenance so stale locks can be detected, and discarding abandoned locks after a timeout.

queries.query: what keeps the same relationship from being stored twice
queries.why: store.go records that edges sharing a fingerprint are stored once; walker.go records preventing overlapping captures from emitting duplicate edges. The duplicate can be born in either place.

queries.query: what makes the order files are parsed the same on every build
queries.why: build.go records keeping deterministic input sequencing separate from concurrent parsing, and preserving file order before parsing starts.

queries.query: why does an answer with nothing in it still suggest another call
queries.why: handler_intent.go records turning an empty answer into a step rather than a dead end; handler_query.go carries the same hand-off on the search side.

queries.query: why must the database schema be migrated before the server will run
queries.why: migrate.go records keeping schema changes out of normal runtime startup, and migration.go holds the version guard that refuses an older database.

queries.query: 네임스페이스 설정이 플래그 기본값에 가려지지 않게 하는 곳은 어디야
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose: search answers questions written in English. Supporting Korean means teaching the query pipeline Korean morphology — splitting the particle off 파일을 so it can reach 파일 — and a Korean function-word list to mirror the English one in queryterm. Neither generalises to the next language a user types in, and gorm, cobra and context-diary hold no Hangul, so the only evidence for such a change would be the four ccg queries it was written against: the exact overfit README.md forbids. This one is declined with the other three even though it scores today — 6 of its 9 scored terms reach a recorded reason, which is what carries it past CanAnswer where the others fail. Declining only the failures would be fitting the rule to the results. It is not in zeroScoreNotes because it does not score zero, and the ratchet still guards it: root.go records resolving namespace precedence between config and the --namespace flag default, its reason is written in Korean, and prefix matching reaches it — '네임스페이스'* still matches '네임스페이스가' — at rank 1. A sanitizer change that drops prefixes would silently break every Korean reason in the graph, and this entry is what catches that.

queries.query: why does an invoice get a loyalty discount
queries.why: nothing in this codebase is about invoices, loyalty, or discounts, so the right answer is nothing at all. It used to return two files: 'get' survived the function-word list and prefix matching then reached getAnnotation, getImpactRadius, and getAffectedFlows spelled inside recorded reasons. Narrowing short Latin terms to exact matches closed that, and the question stays as the guard on it.

queries.query: why did the build refuse a source file that changed while it was being opened
queries.why: fileio.go의 openRegularSourceFile 구현은 열기 전후의 파일 정보를 비교하고 같은 파일이 아니면 읽기를 중단한다. 파일 교체 경쟁 중 심볼릭 링크나 다른 파일을 따라가지 않게 하는 진입점이다.

queries.query: why did one oversized file abort indexing before it was read
queries.why: fileio.go의 크기 검사 구현은 파일 내용을 메모리에 올리기 전에 개별 파일 한도를 비교해 오류를 반환한다. 색인 중 큰 파일 하나가 즉시 실패를 만든 원인을 추적하기 좋은 자리다.

queries.query: why did an update merely warn about unreadable files instead of failing
queries.why: update.go는 읽기 실패를 모아 경고한 뒤 설정이 켜진 경우에만 오류로 승격한다. fileio.go는 누락 경로 집계와 단일 구조화 오류 변환을 담당하므로 둘 다 판단 흐름의 시작점이다.

queries.query: why did change analysis fail after a huge diff exhausted the command output limit
queries.why: git.go의 실행 구현은 diff 표준 출력을 제한된 리더로 읽고 최대 바이트를 넘으면 오류를 반환한다. 변경 분석이 큰 diff에서 멈춘 이유를 직접 확인할 수 있다.

queries.query: why was the wiki index never left half-written after the process died
queries.why: wiki.go는 같은 디렉터리의 임시 파일에 전체 JSON을 기록하고 닫은 다음 최종 경로로 이름을 바꾼다. 독자가 중간 스냅샷을 보지 않는 이유를 확인할 수 있다.

queries.query: why is a cross-project link still dead after the target project was rebuilt
queries.why: service.go는 한 네임스페이스가 다시 만들어진 뒤 그쪽을 가리키는 외부 행을 다시 해석하고 상태나 대상 노드가 달라지면 갱신한다. 재빌드 뒤 링크 복구가 안 된 장애의 시작점이다.

queries.query: what made readiness fail while webhook work kept piling up
queries.why: serve.go의 준비 상태 검사는 추적 중인 저장소 수가 한도에 닿거나 대기·처리 시간이 허용 시간을 넘으면 실패를 반환한다. 큐 적체가 트래픽 차단으로 이어지는 판정이 모여 있다.

queries.query: why does status stay degraded after the latest repository sync failed
queries.why: serve.go는 마지막 오류 시각이 마지막 성공보다 새로우면 전체 또는 저장소별 상태를 degraded로 둔다. 이후 성공이 오류를 덮기 전까지 상태가 회복되지 않는 이유를 보여준다.

queries.query: why did an incremental update lose relationships between files read in different batches
queries.why: incremental.go는 모든 배치의 노드를 먼저 저장한 뒤 별도 스풀에서 관계를 해석하며, update.go는 그 staged 경로를 선택해 재생한다. 배치 경계를 넘는 관계가 사라진 회귀를 조사할 두 진입점이다.

queries.query: why are unchanged files skipped without calling a parser again
queries.why: incremental.go의 동기화 루프는 저장된 해시와 새 해시가 같고 강제 처리가 아니면 파서를 고르기만 한 뒤 내용을 해제하고 건너뛴다. 재파싱 여부가 결정되는 구현이다.

queries.query: why do uncertain call targets appear in a flow unless I opt out
queries.why: flow.go는 별도 선택이 없으면 불확실한 대체 호출 관계를 포함하도록 기본값을 채우고, 명시적으로 제외했을 때만 해당 관계를 건너뛴다. 흐름 결과가 넓어지는 이유가 여기에 있다.

queries.query: why does impact include code on both sides of a relationship
queries.why: impact.go의 너비 우선 탐색은 각 깊이에서 나가는 관계와 들어오는 관계를 모두 읽어 다음 방문 목록에 넣는다. 영향 범위가 의존 대상과 의존 주체 양쪽으로 퍼지는 구현이다.

queries.query: why does editing a function with many outgoing links rank as riskier
queries.why: service.go의 위험도 계산은 수정 구간이 겹친 횟수에 해당 노드의 바깥 관계 수에 1을 더한 값을 곱한다. 같은 변경량이어도 연결이 많은 코드가 위로 가는 이유를 보여준다.

queries.query: why does the wiki tree fetch only the requested number of levels
queries.why: builder.go는 요청한 깊이까지만 현재 노드의 자식을 재귀적으로 채우고 경계에 도달하면 빈 자식 목록을 둔다. 전체 트리를 매번 만들지 않는 탐색 흐름의 시작점이다.

queries.query: why does a configured clone host take precedence over the address in a webhook
queries.why: cloneurl.go는 유효한 기본 주소 중 첫 번째가 있으면 저장소 경로를 붙여 즉시 반환하고, 기본 주소가 전혀 없고 허용 설정이 있을 때만 payload 주소를 사용한다. 선택 순서를 직접 읽을 수 있다.

queries.query: why does an exact short name jump ahead of stronger text matches
queries.why: sanitize.go는 단일 식별자 모양의 질의만 정확 이름 승격 대상으로 만들고 일치 항목을 맨 앞으로 옮긴다. postgres.go와 sqlite.go는 각 검색 결과에 이 후처리를 적용하므로 어느 백엔드에서든 읽기 시작할 수 있다.

queries.query: why can searching for a language name find files that only carry an extension
queries.why: document.go의 문서 구성은 파일명 확장자를 토큰으로 넣고 짧은 확장자를 사람이 쓰는 언어 이름으로도 확장한다. 경로에 긴 언어명이 없어도 검색되는 이유다.

queries.query: why are only reasons and rules searchable in the intent index
queries.why: document.go의 별도 색인 내용 생성 루프는 어노테이션 태그 중 의도와 도메인 규칙 종류만 이어 붙이고 나머지는 건너뛴다. 일반 심볼 정보와 이유 전용 색인이 갈리는 코드다.

queries.query: what decides whether an HTTP server may listen outside the local machine without authentication
queries.why: serve.go의 노출 검사는 로컬 주소이거나 명시적 비보안 허용이면 통과시키고, 그 밖의 주소에는 인증 토큰을 요구한다. 외부 바인딩 허용 여부를 결정하는 정책 지점이다.

queries.query: what prevents a user supplied revision from being treated as a command option
queries.why: git.go는 호출자가 준 기준 리비전이 비었거나 하이픈으로 시작하면 명령 실행 전에 거부하고, 경로 인수 앞에는 옵션 종료 표식도 넣는다. 외부 입력이 명령 옵션으로 해석되지 않게 하는 자리다.

queries.query: what limits how much source code a single indexing pass may read
queries.why: fileio.go에는 한 파일의 바이트 수와 이번 실행에서 누적한 바이트 수를 각각 설정 한도와 비교하는 검사가 있다. 메모리에 읽을 수 있는 소스 규모 정책의 중심이다.

queries.query: 읽지 못한 파일을 업데이트에서 삭제된 것으로 보지 않는 기준은 어디야
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose: search answers questions written in English. Supporting Korean means teaching the query pipeline Korean morphology — splitting the particle off 파일을 so it can reach 파일 — and a Korean function-word list to mirror the English one in queryterm. Neither generalises to the next language a user types in, and gorm, cobra and context-diary hold no Hangul, so the only evidence for such a change would be the four ccg queries it was written against: the exact overfit README.md forbids. Measured: 2 of the 10 scored terms appear in any recorded reason, so CanAnswer drops all 5 intent hits and the answer is empty. 파일을 scores 3 in this corpus where 파일 scores 22. The judgment itself still stands — update.go는 현재 파일 집합에 없더라도 읽기 실패 집합에 들어 있는 기존 경로는 삭제 목록에서 제외한다. 일시적인 접근 실패를 실제 삭제로 오인하지 않는 판정 코드다.

queries.query: 여러 묶음으로 읽은 파일 사이의 호출 관계는 왜 마지막에 한꺼번에 연결하지
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose: search answers questions written in English. Supporting Korean means teaching the query pipeline Korean morphology — splitting the particle off 파일을 so it can reach 파일 — and a Korean function-word list to mirror the English one in queryterm. Neither generalises to the next language a user types in, and gorm, cobra and context-diary hold no Hangul, so the only evidence for such a change would be the four ccg queries it was written against: the exact overfit README.md forbids. Measured: 2 of the 11 scored terms appear in any recorded reason, so CanAnswer drops all 30 intent hits and the answer is empty. Only 파일 and 호출 score at all; the other nine terms carry a particle or an ending. The judgment itself still stands — incremental.go는 모든 배치의 노드 저장과 삭제를 끝낸 뒤 관계 스풀을 다시 읽어 구현 관계와 나머지 관계를 순서대로 해석한다. update.go는 이 staged 동기화 경로를 호출하므로 둘 다 자연스러운 출발점이다.

queries.query: which team owns the changed code and should review it
queries.why: 저장소에는 변경 위험과 그래프 관계 분석은 있지만 코드 소유권 파일, blame 이력, 리뷰어 배정 기능이 없다. 코드 분석 제품에는 그럴듯하지만 이 코드베이스에서는 빈 결과가 정상이다.

queries.query: which functions consume the most CPU in a live process
queries.why: 이 도구는 정적 파싱과 저장된 그래프를 다루며 실행 중 프로세스의 CPU 프로파일을 수집하거나 함수별 샘플을 집계하지 않는다. 따라서 답이 없어야 한다.

queries.query: which dependencies have known vulnerabilities or forbidden licenses
queries.why: 의존 관계 파싱 기능은 있어도 취약점 데이터베이스 조회, SBOM 생성, 라이선스 허용 목록 검사는 구현되어 있지 않다. 보안 분석 도구에서 기대할 법한 주제지만 여기서는 음성 사례다.

queries.query: why are old generated pages still present after their source files were removed
queries.why: generator.go의 실행 흐름은 정리 옵션이 켜졌을 때만 이전 manifest와 현재 산출물을 비교해 오래된 페이지를 지운다.

queries.query: why are handwritten pages kept when obsolete generated docs are pruned
queries.why: generator.go의 정리 루프는 이전 manifest에 있던 파일이라도 생성기 표식으로 시작하지 않으면 삭제하지 않는다.

queries.query: what decides whether generated documentation may delete an existing page
queries.why: generator.go는 이전 manifest에는 있으나 현재 목록에는 없는 파일만 후보로 삼고, 실제 내용이 생성기 표식으로 시작할 때만 제거한다.

queries.query: 코드가 바뀐 뒤 어떤 주석을 다시 확인해야 하는지는 어디서 판단해
queries.why: Deliberately unsupported, kept red on purpose: search answers questions written in English. Supporting Korean means teaching the query pipeline Korean morphology — splitting the particle off 파일을 so it can reach 파일 — and a Korean function-word list to mirror the English one in queryterm. Neither generalises to the next language a user types in, and gorm, cobra and context-diary hold no Hangul, so the only evidence for such a change would be the four ccg queries it was written against: the exact overfit README.md forbids. Measured: 4 of the 10 scored terms appear in any recorded reason — still under half — so CanAnswer drops all 9 intent hits and the answer is empty. The judgment itself still stands — lint.go는 심볼 갱신 시각과 어노테이션 갱신 시각을 비교해 코드가 더 새로우면 드리프트로 보고한다.

scoring.note: One question set, two tools. `search` is replayed by golden_test.go against candidates.json; `wiki_search` by golden_docs_test.go against docs_candidates.json. Sharing the questions is the point: a number is only comparable if both tools were asked the same thing.
scoring.out_of_scope: Names the tools that have decided not to answer a query, so their zero is a recorded decision rather than a defect. A query stays in the set, and stays red, for every tool that lists itself here.
